title: How to Visit Marlborough & Blenheim on a Family Budget
meta_desc: Discover how a family of four can enjoy Marlborough and Blenheim for $180‑$300 a day with free activities, budget stays, smart savings and splurge‑worthy experiences.
intro: Marlborough’s sunny vineyards, crystal‑clear Sounds and friendly towns make it a perfect family getaway. With a bit of planning you can soak up wildlife cruises, short Queen Charlotte Track walks and beach fun without breaking the bank.

sections.heading: Getting There & Getting Around
sections.body:
Most families arrive via the Interislander or Bluebridge ferry into Picton. From there it’s a short 30‑minute drive to Blenheim – the region’s main hub – and a further 45‑minute drive to Momorangi Bay. Renting a compact car costs about $70‑$90 per day, fuel around $1.80/L, so budget $15‑$20 daily for petrol.

Driving is the cheapest way to reach the scattered beaches and trailheads; public buses run between Picton and Blenheim for $8 adult, $4 child each way, but they’re infrequent.

Where to Stay – Budget to Mid‑range
body
Accommodation drives the daily budget. For families of four
consider these options that sit comfortably within the $180‑$300
/day range.</

p>

Cheapest: Holiday parks such as Marlborough Holiday Park (Picton) or Blenheim Top 10 Holiday Park offer 2‑bed cabins at $120‑$150 per night
kitchen facilities and playgrounds. Mid‑range: Boutique motels like the Picton Harbour Motel ($180‑$220) or Blenheim

s Chateau Marlborough ($200‑$250) provide private bathrooms and breakfast options. Splurge‑free tip – book a cabin with a kitchen and self‑cater for breakfast and dinner; a grocery shop for four costs roughly $60‑$80 per day.<

Marlborough shines when you look beyond the pricey wine tours. The best memories are often free: a splash in the crystal‑clear Pelorus Bridge swimming hole, a wander through the Pelorus Bridge Scenic Reserve, or a play session at the Waitohi Foreshore playground. All are suitable for kids 5+ and require no entry fee.</

p>

Low‑cost options include the Edwin Fox Maritime Museum ($10 adult
$5 child) and a short 2‑hour family‑friendly section of the Queen Charlotte Track – start at the Queen Charlotte Lookout and return via the loop; the walk is about 4km
takes 1.5‑2 hours and offers stunning harbour views.<

While you can fill most days with free fun, a few experiences truly elevate the trip and are worth budgeting for. The dolphin‑watch cruise from Picton ($55 adult, $35 child, 2‑hour tour) guarantees sightings of bottlenose dolphins, seals and occasional whales – a thrill for kids and adults alike. Sea kayaking in the Marlborough Sounds ($80 per double‑kayak for 2 hours) lets the family explore hidden coves; most operators provide life‑jackets and brief instruction.</
